fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. Amos says he sees a basket of summer fruit, and the LORD answers, "The end has come for My people Israel; I will no longer spare them." (Amos 8:2) Amos was just asked a simple question, and the answer was this. I think that basket stopped looking so pretty to him right then.

Cheering is the opposite direction, friend. The songs of the temple turn the other way, and the Lord GOD says they "…will turn to wailing." (Amos 8:3) I think this is a heavy verse, because it also speaks of many corpses.

Right on. They ask, "When will the New Moon be over, that we may sell grain?" (Amos 8:5) The New Moon and the Sabbath are in their way, and they're watching for when they end. I think this is a heavy verse, because their plan is to cheat people.

True, friend. They say, "Let us reduce the ephah and increase the shekel; let us cheat with dishonest scales." (Amos 8:5) That's three tricks in one sentence. I think this is a heavy part, because it's a plan to cheat people.

The Nile, friend. The land will "…swell like the Nile; it will surge and then subside like the Nile in Egypt." (Amos 8:8) That river rises and falls, and the whole land is pictured doing the same. Big movement, all of it swelling and surging.

An old friend is a sad loss, friend, but it isn't what the verse says. The LORD says, "I will make it like a time of mourning for an only son, and its outcome like a bitter day." (Amos 8:10) The mourning is compared to the mourning for an only son.

That's the one, friend. The LORD says of those who swear by Samaria's guilt, Dan's god and the way of Beersheba, "…they will fall, never to rise again." (Amos 8:14) That's the end of the passage. I think it's a serious way to close.
